issues.legal_issue: A reviewing court exceeds its revisional authority when, on a private party’s challenge to an acquittal, it reappraises evidence and overturns factual findings without an error of law, even if it orders a retrial rather than entering a conviction.
material_facts: The trial court acquitted the accused after examining the prosecution evidence and finding the prosecution’s account unreliable, including because of its assessment of the alleged cultivation and harvesting and discrepancies in the witnesses’ evidence.
A private complainant sought revision of the acquittal.
The reviewing court reappraised the evidence, disagreed with the trial court’s factual findings, described the acquittal as perverse, and ordered a retrial without convicting the accused.
The reviewing court did not identify an error of law in the trial court’s findings.
issues.conclusion: The reviewing court exceeded its revisional powers. Its retrial order was set aside and the trial court’s acquittal restored.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 439(1) and 439(4) of the Criminal Procedure Code, 1898, the High Court may exercise specified appellate powers in revision, but may not convert an acquittal into a conviction. Section 439(4) does not permit the High Court, in a private party’s revision against an acquittal, to evade that limitation by reappraising evidence and reversing factual findings without an error on a point of law, merely by ordering a retrial instead of convicting the accused. Calling the trial judgment perverse or lacking perspective does not itself justify that reappraisal. The judgment cites no earlier cases for this principle.

rule.if: private_revision_against_acquittal and trial_acquittal_based_on_evidence and no_error_of_law_identified and reviewing_court_reappraises_factual_findings and reviewing_court_orders_retrial and reviewing_court_does_not_convict

predicates.private_revision_against_acquittal: A private party seeks review of a decision acquitting the accused.
predicates.trial_acquittal_based_on_evidence: The trial court acquits the accused after assessing the evidence.
predicates.no_error_of_law_identified: The reviewing court identifies no error of law in the trial court’s decision.
predicates.reviewing_court_reappraises_factual_find: The reviewing court reassesses the evidence and disagrees with factual findings underlying the acquittal.
predicates.reviewing_court_orders_retrial: The reviewing court directs that the accused be tried again.
predicates.reviewing_court_does_not_convict: The reviewing court orders a retrial without itself convicting the accused.
predicates.retrial_order_exceeds_revisional_authori: The reviewing court’s retrial order exceeds its authority in revision.

issues.definition: When a private party challenges an evidence-based acquittal, no error of law is identified, and the reviewing court reappraises the factual findings and orders a retrial without convicting the accused, the retrial order exceeds revisional authority.
